category: Component & library management: library projects, database libraries, symbol/footprint editing, managed (Altium 365) content
description: Library package projects and integrated libraries, database and SVN database libraries, schematic-library and PCB-library editor commands, component types and model links, and the managed-component features of an Altium 365 Workspace (templates, lifecycles, revisions, where-used, migration, supply chain).

tools.name: Library Package project (.LibPkg)
tools.description: Project type that groups schematic libraries (.SchLib), PCB libraries (.PcbLib), simulation and 3D model files so they can be compiled into a single Integrated Library (.IntLib). Created with File > New > Project > Integrated Library; compiled with Project > Compile Integrated Library, which validates every model link and writes the .IntLib to the project output folder.
tools.usage: File > New > Project > Integrated Library (.LibPkg); Project > Add Existing to Project (.SchLib/.PcbLib); Project > Compile Integrated Library

parameters.name: Output path
parameters.description: Project Options > Options > Output Path for the .IntLib.

tools.example: Create Company.LibPkg, add Passives.SchLib and Passives.PcbLib, compile: Company.IntLib appears and is auto-installed in the Components panel.
tools.notes: Compile errors list missing footprints/models in the Messages panel; fix the symbol's model links before shipping the .IntLib.

tools.name: Integrated Library (.IntLib) compile and extract
tools.description: Read-only compiled library bundling symbols with their footprints and models. Built from a .LibPkg (Project > Compile Integrated Library); editing requires opening the .IntLib (File > Open) and choosing Extract Sources, which recreates the .LibPkg with .SchLib/.PcbLib in a sub-folder. The Library Options project tab selects Original or Altium Designer format.
tools.usage: Project > Compile Integrated Library; File > Open <name>.IntLib > Extract Sources
tools.example: Open Miscellaneous Devices.IntLib > Extract Sources, edit the LED symbol, recompile to a new .IntLib in the company path.
tools.notes: Installed integrated libraries are listed in Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries (Installed tab).

tools.name: Database Library (.DbLib) field mappings
tools.description: A .DbLib links an external database (ODBC/OLE DB, Access, Excel, SQL Server) to symbols and footprints: the Database Library document defines the connection string, the tables/views to use, the Field Settings (Database Key, Symbol Reference, Footprint fields) and the Field Mappings that map database columns to component parameters (Design parameter / Add To Design / Update Values options). Parts are placed from the Components panel with parameters pulled live from the database.
tools.usage: File > New > Library > Database Library; set Source of Connection, Table Browser, Field Settings, Field Mappings; install via Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries

parameters.name: Connection string / Data Link file
parameters.description: ODBC/OLE DB source.

parameters.name: Database key field
parameters.description: Unique column that identifies each record (e.g. PartNumber).

parameters.name: Symbol Reference / Footprint Ref / Footprint Path fields
parameters.description: Columns naming the SchLib symbol and PcbLib footprint(s).

parameters.name: Field Mappings
parameters.description: Column -> parameter with Add To Design / Update Values / Visible On Add flags.

tools.example: Excel workbook with sheet 'Resistors' (PartNumber, Value, Symbol=RES, Footprint=0603, Manufacturer); map Value to Comment and Manufacturer to parameter; place from the Components panel.
tools.notes: Symbols/footprints must be reachable via library search paths defined in the .DbLib's Library Search Path field; use Tools > Update From Libraries / Update Parameters From Database to refresh placed parts.

tools.name: SVN Database Library (.SVNDbLib) and Database Link (.DBLink)
tools.description: .SVNDbLib extends the database library by pulling symbols and footprints from a Subversion repository (version-controlled .SchLib/.PcbLib files) with the database supplying parameters; .DBLink does not place parts but links already-placed components to database records by a key field so their parameters can be updated from the database.
tools.usage: File > New > Library > SVN Database Library / Database Link file; Tools > Update Parameters From Database (schematic)

parameters.name: Repository / working folder
parameters.description: SVN path and local checkout used by the SVNDbLib (Preferences > Data Management > SVN Libraries).

parameters.name: Key field
parameters.description: Parameter matched against the database key for DBLink.

tools.example: Add Company.DBLink to the project, Tools > Update Parameters From Database: all parts with a matching PartNumber get refreshed Manufacturer/Description fields.
tools.notes: Altium 365 managed components are the recommended successor to SVNDbLib.

tools.name: Tools > Update From Libraries (schematic)
tools.description: Compares placed components with their source libraries and updates symbol graphics, pins, parameters and model links according to the chosen options (Update Symbol Graphics/Pins, Update Parameters with Add/Remove/Update choices, Update Model Links), producing an ECO-style change list. Used after editing library symbols or migrating parameter sets.
tools.usage: Tools > Update From Libraries... > select components/libraries > Update Parameters / Graphics options > Next > Execute

parameters.name: Parameter actions
parameters.description: Add new, Remove deleted, Update values per parameter.

parameters.name: Model links
parameters.description: Replace footprint/sim links from library.

tools.example: After adding a 'Manufacturer' parameter to all resistor symbols, Tools > Update From Libraries with 'Add parameters that exist in library only' pushes it to every placed resistor.
tools.notes: Library must be available (installed or project library); database parts use Update Parameters From Database instead.

tools.name: Schematic Library editor: Tools > New Component / Rename / Remove / Copy / Paste
tools.description: Component-level commands of the .SchLib editor: New Component (dialog for name; creates an empty symbol with the default part), Rename Component, Remove Component, Copy Component (to another open library), Duplicate; the SCH Library panel lists components, their parts (Add Part / Remove Part for multi-part symbols), pins and models. Tools > Component Properties opens the Properties panel with Designator prefix, Comment, Description, Parameters and Models.
tools.usage: Schematic Library editor: Tools > New Component | Rename Component | Remove Component | Copy Component | New Part | Remove Part; SCH Library panel

parameters.name: Component name
parameters.description: Library reference (LibRef) of the symbol.

parameters.name: Parts
parameters.description: Sub-parts A, B, C... of multi-part components.

tools.example: Tools > New Component 'LM358', Tools > New Part twice for the two op-amps, draw each part with pins 1-3 and 5-7, share power pins 4/8 as hidden pins.
tools.notes: Set Designator to 'U?' and Default Comment; Symbol Wizard builds rectangular symbols from a pin table.

tools.name: Pin properties (electrical type, symbols, hidden pins, pin swapping)
tools.description: Each library pin has Designator, Name (with overline via backslash after each character), Electrical Type (Input, I/O, Output, Open Collector, Passive, HiZ, Open Emitter, Power), Description, Pin Length, Orientation, Hide (hidden pins auto-connect to the net named in Name, e.g. VCC/GND), Symbols (Inside, Inside Edge, Outside, Outside Edge: Clock, Dot/Inverted, Active Low Input/Output...), Pin/Part Swapping group and Font settings. Electrical types feed the Connection Matrix checks and Signal Integrity.
tools.usage: Schematic Library editor: double-click pin > Properties panel; SCH Library panel > Pins list > Edit; Place > Pin (P P), Tab to set before placing

parameters.name: Electrical Type
parameters.description: Drives ERC connection matrix.

parameters.name: Hide / Name
parameters.description: Hidden power pins connect implicitly to the net named by Name.

parameters.name: Symbols
parameters.description: IEEE-style graphics inside/outside the pin.

tools.example: Pin 8 'VCC', Electrical Type Power, Hide enabled: the part draws power from net VCC automatically; enable Show Hidden Pins on the placed part to verify.
tools.notes: Hidden power pins are a classic source of silent net merges; prefer visible power pins on new symbols.

tools.name: Place > IEEE Symbols (schematic library)
tools.description: Library editor menu of IEEE/ANSI graphical symbols (Dot, Right Left Signal Flow, Clock, Active Low Input, Analog Signal In, Not Logic Connection, Postponed Output, Open Collector, HiZ, High Current, Pulse, Delay, Group Line, Group Binary, Active Low Output, Pi Symbol, Greater/Less Equal, Sigma, Schmitt, Open Collector Pull Up, Open Emitter, Open Emitter Pull Up, Digital Signal In, Shift Left, Open Output, Left Right Signal Flow, Bidirectional Signal Flow) placed as standalone graphics; pin-attached variants are set in Pin Properties > Symbols.
tools.usage: Schematic Library editor: Place > IEEE Symbols > <symbol>; resize with + / - while placing
tools.example: Place > IEEE Symbols > Schmitt inside the body of a Schmitt-trigger inverter symbol.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsSymbol finds these objects.

tools.name: Component types (Standard, Mechanical, Graphical, Net Tie, Jumper, Standard (No BOM))
tools.description: The Type property of a component controls synchronisation and BOM behaviour: Standard (normal), Mechanical (no schematic symbol required; may exist only on PCB, appears in BOM), Graphical (documentation only, not synchronised or in BOM), Net Tie / Net Tie (In BOM) (footprint copper intentionally shorts nets; DRC allows it), Jumper (nets joined at PCB level via jumper wires), Standard (No BOM) (synchronised but excluded from BOM). Set in the library or on the placed part.
tools.usage: Component Properties panel > General > Type (schematic or PCB); query ComponentType / IsNetTieComponent etc.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Standard | Mechanical | Graphical | Net Tie | Net Tie (In BOM) | Jumper | Standard (No BOM).

tools.example: Set the analog/digital ground bridge footprint to Net Tie so the shorting copper is not flagged; enable Verify Shorting Copper in DRC.
tools.notes: Mechanical parts placed only on the PCB survive Design > Update PCB ECOs without being removed.

tools.name: PCB Library editor: Tools > New Blank Component / Component Properties / Copy / Paste Component
tools.description: Footprint-level commands of the .PcbLib editor: New Blank Component (prompts for name), Component Properties (name, height, description, area/type), Remove Component, Copy / Paste Component between libraries, Next/Prev Component, Place Component from library, and the PCB Library panel listing footprints, primitives and 3D models with filter/mask. Tools > Component Wizard and IPC Compliant Footprint Wizard generate footprints parametrically.
tools.usage: PCB Library editor: Tools > New Blank Component | Component Properties | Remove Component | Copy | Paste Component; PCB Library panel

parameters.name: Name / Description / Height
parameters.description: Footprint metadata (Height feeds Height rules when no 3D body exists).

tools.example: Tools > New Blank Component 'SOT23-3', place three pads with Place > Pad, courtyard on Mechanical 15, 3D body via Place > 3D Body > STEP.
tools.notes: Edit > Set Reference > Pin 1 / Center / Location sets the footprint origin; Reports > Component Rule Check validates pads/names.

tools.name: Pad Via Library (.PvLib) and pad/via templates
tools.description: Templates that define complete pad or via definitions (size, hole, shape, mask expansions, IPC-4761 features) stored locally in a PCB document or in a shared Pad Via Library (.PvLib) file installed like other libraries. The Pad Via Templates panel (PCB panel mode) and Properties panel let pads/vias be linked to a template so changes propagate; Routing Via Style rules can be set to Template preferred mode.
tools.usage: File > New > Library > Pad Via Library; PCB panel > Pad & Via Templates; Properties panel > Template drop-down; Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries to install

parameters.name: Template name
parameters.description: e.g. v30h15 (via 0.30 mm hole 0.15 mm).

parameters.name: Library / Local
parameters.description: Template source.

tools.example: Create Company.PvLib with via templates uVia_0.2, Thru_0.3, Thru_0.5; in the Routing Via Style rule choose Template preferred and enable them.
tools.notes: Query keywords IsLinkedToPadViaTemplate / IsLinkedToPadViaLibrary audit usage.

tools.name: Place > 3D Body (Extruded, Cylinder, Sphere, Generic STEP) in the PCB Library
tools.description: Adds 3D bodies to a footprint: Extruded (draw an outline, set overall height and standoff), Cylinder, Sphere, or Generic 3D Model (embed or link a STEP/Parasolid file with Model Search / Model Selection, rotation X/Y/Z and standoff height). Bodies drive 3D visualisation, Component Clearance/Height rules, STEP export and MCAD CoDesigner.
tools.usage: PCB Library editor: Place > 3D Body > Extruded / Cylinder / Sphere / Generic 3D Model (Properties: Source Embedded/Link, Rotation, Standoff Height)

parameters.name: Overall Height / Standoff Height
parameters.description: Extruded body dimensions.

parameters.name: Model file
parameters.description: STEP (.step/.stp) or Parasolid (.x_t) source.

tools.example: Place > 3D Body > Generic 3D Model, Embed 'SOT23.step', rotate X 90 so the body sits on the pads, standoff 0.05 mm.
tools.notes: Snap the body to pads with the 3D-body Snap Points; 3D body layer is usually Mechanical 13 (or the Component Body layer type).

tools.name: Model search paths and model linking (Footprint / Simulation / SI / PCB3D models)
tools.description: A schematic component's Models list links model types: Footprint (PcbLib, with Any / Library name / Library path / Use footprint from integrated library location modes), Simulation (SIM), Signal Integrity (SI), PCB3D (legacy) and Ibis. Models are resolved through installed libraries, project libraries and search paths (Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries > Search Path tab; Project Options > Search Paths). The Footprint Manager gives a project-wide view.
tools.usage: Component Properties > Models > Add (Footprint / Simulation / Signal Integrity); PCB Model dialog > Browse; Tools > Footprint Manager

parameters.name: PCB Library location
parameters.description: Any | Library name | Library path | Use footprint from component library ...

parameters.name: Footprint name
parameters.description: Must match the PcbLib component name exactly.

tools.example: Add footprint 0603 from Passives.PcbLib with location 'Any' so any installed library holding 0603 satisfies it during ECO.
tools.notes: 'Any' resolution can silently pick a different library's footprint; use Library name for controlled libraries.

tools.name: Components panel: filters, columns and placement options
tools.description: Unified panel for searching and placing parts from file libraries, database libraries and the connected Workspace: library/category selector, text search with parameter filters (Categories, Manufacturer, Lifecycle, Parameters facets), configurable columns, Details/Models/Part Choices/Where Used/Supply Chain tabs for the selected component, drag-and-drop or Place button, and right-click commands (Place, Edit, Operations such as Release/Clone, Update to the latest revision for managed parts, Add to project, Download to a file library).
tools.usage: View > Panels > Components; choose library or Workspace; type filter; drag part onto the sheet

parameters.name: Filter / Facets
parameters.description: Text search plus parameter-based filtering.

parameters.name: Columns
parameters.description: Right-click header > Select Columns.

tools.example: Select the Workspace, filter 'Capacitor 100nF 0402 X7R', check Supply Chain tab for stock, drag onto the schematic.
tools.notes: File-based libraries appear only when installed (Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries) or added to the project.

tools.name: Manufacturer Part Search: Acquire / Import to Workspace and library
tools.description: The Manufacturer Part Search panel (Octopart/IHS-backed) finds manufacturer parts with datasheets, pricing, stock and, where available, ready-made symbol/footprint/3D models; the Acquire command creates a managed component in the Workspace (or a file-library component via Download to local library) with parameters, part choice and models populated. Parts without models can be paired with generic templates.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Manufacturer Part Search > search > select part > Acquire (Workspace) or Download (file library) / Place

parameters.name: Component template
parameters.description: Workspace template applied on acquire (parameter set, folder, naming).

parameters.name: Models
parameters.description: Symbol/footprint/3D sourced from the part data when offered.

tools.example: Search 'STM32F405RGT6', click the part, Acquire with template 'Microcontrollers': a managed component with symbol, footprint and part choice is created and can be placed.
tools.notes: Requires sign-in and internet access; Parts Providers preferences control suppliers and currency.

tools.name: Symbol/footprint import from vendor generators (Ultra Librarian, SnapEDA, SamacSys / Component Search Engine)
tools.description: Third-party CAD model services provide Altium-format symbols and footprints: Ultra Librarian and SnapEDA offer downloads as .SchLib/.PcbLib (or .IntLib) that are opened and copied into company libraries, while SamacSys' Component Search Engine/Library Loader can push parts directly into open Altium libraries. Altium's own Manufacturer Part Search also surfaces such models where available. Always run Reports > Component Rule Check and review pad sizes against IPC before use.
tools.usage: Download the Altium package from the vendor site > File > Open the .SchLib/.PcbLib > Tools > Copy Component into the company library (or Library Loader push)
tools.example: SnapEDA part 'LM2596S-ADJ' downloaded as Altium zip; open LM2596S.SchLib and .PcbLib, copy both into PowerICs.SchLib/PcbLib, relink the footprint model with Library name mode.
tools.notes: Vendor footprints vary in origin/orientation conventions (IPC-7351 vs manufacturer); normalise pin-1 orientation and courtyard layers to the company standard.

tools.name: Component templates (Workspace CMPT)
tools.description: Managed component templates define, per component type, the required/optional parameters (with defaults, units and value lists), the default folder, naming/revision schemes and default models, so components created in the Workspace (via Component Editor, Manufacturer Part Search Acquire or Library Migrator) are consistent. Managed under Explorer panel > Templates > Component Templates and Preferences > Data Management > Component Types.
tools.usage: Explorer panel > Templates > Component Templates > New; Component Editor (Batch mode) > Template column

parameters.name: Parameters
parameters.description: Name, type (text/number/enum), required flag, default.

parameters.name: Default folder / naming scheme
parameters.description: Where and how new components are stored.

tools.example: Template 'Resistors': parameters Value (required), Tolerance, Power, Package; naming CMP-{0000}; folder Components/Resistors.
tools.notes: Changing a template does not retroactively update existing components; use Batch Component Editing to apply.

tools.name: Component Editor (Single Component / Batch Component Editing modes)
tools.description: The Workspace component editor: Single Component Editing mode shows one managed component with its parameters, symbol, footprints, part choices and template; Batch Component Editing mode presents many components in a spreadsheet for mass creation or edits (paste from Excel, assign models by drag-and-drop from library panes), then Save to Server releases new revisions of every changed item.
tools.usage: Explorer / Components panel > right-click component > Edit; Component Editor > Mode: Single Component Editing / Batch Component Editing; Save to Server

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Single Component Editing | Batch Component Editing.

parameters.name: Save to Server
parameters.description: Releases changed components as new revisions.

tools.example: Batch mode: paste 50 resistor rows (Name, Value, Package) from Excel, assign symbol RES and footprint 0603 to all rows, Save to Server.
tools.notes: Each save creates a revision per the component's revision naming scheme; lifecycle state follows the definition.

tools.name: Lifecycle definitions and revision naming schemes (Workspace)
tools.description: Workspace administrators define lifecycle definitions (states such as New From Design, In Design, Prototype, Production, Obsolete with allowed transitions and colours) and revision naming schemes (e.g. 1-Level Revision Scheme 'A, B, C' or 2-level '1.A') that are assigned per content type (components, symbols, footprints, projects, templates). Component lifecycle appears in the Components panel and ActiveBOM; out-of-date revisions raise Item Manager warnings.
tools.usage: Workspace web UI > Admin > Lifecycle Definitions / Revision Naming Schemes; Preferences > Data Management > Servers > Content Type settings

parameters.name: Lifecycle states / transitions
parameters.description: Named states and permitted changes.

parameters.name: Revision scheme
parameters.description: Pattern for revision IDs.

tools.example: Assign 'Component Lifecycle with Approvals' to Components so a part must be moved to 'Production' before release outputs pass the Component States validation.
tools.notes: Changing a scheme affects only future revisions.

tools.name: Where-used (managed content)
tools.description: For any managed item (component, symbol, footprint, model, template), the Where Used tab of the Explorer/Components panel lists every revision of every project, component or library that references it, enabling impact analysis before obsoleting a part or changing a footprint.
tools.usage: Explorer panel > select item > Where Used tab; Components panel > component > Where Used
tools.example: Before deprecating footprint 'QFN-32_5x5', check Where Used: 14 components across 3 projects reference it - clone and re-link them first.
tools.notes: Only projects saved to the Workspace are indexed.

tools.name: Library Migrator
tools.description: Wizard that converts file-based libraries (.SchLib, .PcbLib, .IntLib, .DbLib) into managed Workspace components: analyses the sources, maps parameters to component templates/types, detects duplicates, extracts manufacturer part numbers into part choices, and releases symbols, footprints and components into Workspace folders. Runs in Simple or Advanced mode with a migration report.
tools.usage: File > Library Migrator (or Components panel > Migrate Libraries); select libraries > Analyze > review mapping > Migrate

parameters.name: Component type mapping
parameters.description: Folder/template per detected type.

parameters.name: Part choice extraction
parameters.description: Parameter that holds the MPN.

tools.example: Migrate Company.IntLib: 1200 components released to Components/<Type> folders with part choices from 'Manufacturer Part Number'.
tools.notes: Run a Component Rule Check on sources first; migration cannot be undone except by deleting items.

tools.name: Managed sheets, templates and Workspace design reuse
tools.description: Besides components, the Workspace stores schematic templates (.SchDot), PCB templates (.PcbDot), Draftsman templates, project templates, OutJob templates, BOM templates and managed schematic sheets (reusable sub-circuits placed as sheet symbols from the Explorer) with revision control. Preferences > Data Management > Templates decides whether local or Workspace templates are used for new documents.
tools.usage: Explorer panel > Templates / Managed Sheets; File > New > Project (from Workspace project templates); Preferences > Data Management > Templates
tools.example: Release 'A3_Landscape' schematic template; new sheets created in any team member's Altium Designer use it automatically.
tools.notes: Managed sheets are read-only when placed; edit and release a new revision, then Update in the consuming projects.

tools.name: Explorer panel folders (Components, Symbols, Footprints, Models, Projects, Templates)
tools.description: Tree view of the connected Workspace (or Altium Enterprise Server): folders for Components (by type), Managed Symbols, Footprints, 3D models, Simulation models, Projects, Templates, Managed Sheets and Datasheets, with item revisions, lifecycle states, Where Used, Preview and supply-chain tabs; supports drag-and-drop placement, Create/Release, Clone, Rename, Delete and folder permissions.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Explorer; sign in to the Workspace; browse folders; right-click items for Operations
tools.example: Explorer > Components > Connectors > right-click USB-C part > Operations > Clone to create a variant with a different footprint.
tools.notes: The Components panel is the preferred search UI; Explorer is for administration and revisions.

tools.name: Reports > Component Rule Check (schematic library)
tools.description: Schematic-library check dialog that scans all components for Duplicate component names, Duplicate pin designators/names, Missing description, Missing footprint/pin name/pin number, Missing default designator, Missing PCB footprint model and Missing model parameters conditions, writing a report with the violating components. Complement to the PCB-library Component Rule Check.
tools.usage: Schematic Library editor: Reports > Component Rule Check... > select checks > OK

parameters.name: Duplicate checks
parameters.description: Component names, pins.

parameters.name: Missing checks
parameters.description: Description, pin name, pin number, footprint, default designator.

tools.example: Run with all checks before compiling the .LibPkg; fix 'Missing Footprint' rows by adding PCB models.
tools.notes: Data Management > Component Rule Checks preferences define the corresponding checks for managed components.

tools.name: Reports > Library Report / Library List (schematic and PCB library)
tools.description: Generates documentation for a library: Library Report (Word/HTML with component images, parameters, pins and models per component; options for graphics and sorting) and Library List (text list of component names/descriptions). PCB libraries offer Reports > Component Report (per footprint) and Library Report.
tools.usage: Schematic Library editor: Reports > Library Report... / Library List; PCB Library editor: Reports > Library Report / Component Report

parameters.name: Format / Contents
parameters.description: Document format and included data (parameters, pins, models, images).

tools.example: Reports > Library Report with 'Include Pins' and 'Show images' for a printed symbol catalogue of Passives.SchLib.
tools.notes: Reports are generated into the library's folder; use for review sign-off of library releases.

tools.name: Height parameter and IPC-7351 footprint naming conventions
tools.description: Footprint Height (Component Properties in the PcbLib or the placed component) is used by Height rules and 3D placeholders when no 3D body exists; IPC-7351 naming (e.g. CAPC1608X90N, SOIC127P600X175-8N, QFN50P500X500X80-33N) encodes pitch, body size and height and is what the IPC Compliant Footprint Wizard produces, with density levels L (Least), N (Nominal), M (Most) selecting land sizes. Consistent naming enables footprint reuse and the Footprint Comparison report.
tools.usage: PCB Library > Component Properties > Height; Tools > IPC Compliant Footprint Wizard (Density Level Most/Nominal/Least)

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: Overall component height.

parameters.name: Density level
parameters.description: L | N | M land-pattern variants.

tools.example: Generate SOIC127P600X175-8N with the IPC wizard, set Height 1.75 mm, add a STEP body, save to Company.PcbLib.
tools.notes: Keep naming suffixes (_N, _M, _L) consistent so rules and BOM cross-references stay predictable.

tools.name: Part choices and supply chain columns (managed components)
tools.description: Each managed component carries Part Choices: an ordered list of manufacturer parts (Manufacturer + MPN) that are acceptable, with optional supplier restrictions. ActiveBOM ranks solutions from these choices using live supplier data (stock, price breaks, lifecycle), and the Components panel Supply Chain tab shows availability. Part choices are edited in the Component Editor or via ActiveBOM > Part Choices column.
tools.usage: Component Editor > Part Choices; Components panel > Part Choices tab; ActiveBOM > Solution column > Edit Part Choices

parameters.name: Manufacturer / Manufacturer Part Number
parameters.description: Approved part.

parameters.name: Rank
parameters.description: Preference order.

tools.example: Add part choices 'Murata GRM155R71C104KA88D' and 'Samsung CL05B104KO5NNNC' to the 100 nF 0402 component; ActiveBOM shows the cheapest in stock.
tools.notes: Parts Providers preferences (Preferences > Data Management > Parts Providers) select suppliers and currency.

tools.name: Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries (Installed / Project / Search Path)
tools.description: Dialog (formerly Available Libraries) with three tabs: Project (libraries added to the current project), Installed (globally installed .IntLib/.SchLib/.PcbLib/.DbLib/.PvLib with Activated checkbox, Move Up/Down for search order, Install/Remove) and Search Path (folders scanned for library files, with Refresh List). Determines what the Components panel offers and how footprints are resolved during ECO.
tools.usage: Preferences > Data Management > File-based Libraries (or Components panel > menu > File-based Libraries Preferences)

parameters.name: Installed list order
parameters.description: Resolution order for footprint lookups with location 'Any'.

parameters.name: Activated
parameters.description: Toggle a library without removing it.

tools.example: Install Company.IntLib and Company.PvLib, move them to the top, deactivate Miscellaneous Devices.IntLib to avoid accidental placements.
tools.notes: Relative paths are stored relative to the Default Locations > Library path.

tools.name: Design > Add/Remove Library (project libraries)
tools.description: Adds .SchLib/.PcbLib/.IntLib/.DbLib files to the project (they appear under Libraries in the Projects panel) so the design is self-contained; project libraries take precedence over installed ones during footprint resolution and are what Make Schematic/PCB Library produce.
tools.usage: Projects panel > right-click project > Add Existing to Project (library files); or Design > Add/Remove Library
tools.example: Add Board_Symbols.SchLib and Board_Footprints.PcbLib to the project before archiving for a contractor.
tools.notes: Project Packager (File > Project Packager) collects project libraries and referenced models into a zip.

tools.name: PCB Library: Tools > Update PCB With Current Footprint / Update PCB With All Footprints
tools.description: Pushes edited footprints from the open .PcbLib into open PCB documents: Update PCB With <footprint> replaces every instance of the current footprint, Update PCB With All Footprints replaces all footprints that exist in the library, showing a Component(s) Update Options dialog (update designators/comments positions, 3D bodies, primitives) and an ECO-style report.
tools.usage: PCB Library editor: Tools > Update PCB With <name> / Update PCB With All Footprints

parameters.name: Update options
parameters.description: Which primitive kinds and text positions to replace.

tools.example: Enlarge the QFN thermal pad in the library, Tools > Update PCB With QFN-32_5x5: all three instances on Main.PcbDoc are refreshed.
tools.notes: Only affects open PCBs; for project-wide updates use the Footprint Manager or an ECO from the schematic.

tools.name: Component Management: Cross-library duplicate check and Component States validation
tools.description: Two validation aids for managed content: the Library Migrator/Component Editor duplicate detection flags components whose parameters or MPN match existing Workspace items; the OutJob Validation output 'Component States' (with Environment Configuration compliance) fails release when placed components use revisions that are not the latest or whose lifecycle is not approved for production.
tools.usage: Output Job > Validation Outputs > Component States; Library Migrator > duplicate report; Item Manager > Choose Latest Revision

parameters.name: Allowed lifecycle states
parameters.description: States accepted by the Component States check.

tools.example: Add Component States to the release OutJob; the Project Releaser stops when U4 is at revision 1.A while 1.B exists.
tools.notes: Item Manager or the Components panel update commands resolve out-of-date revisions.

tools.name: Schematic Library: Tools > Update Schematics / Tools > Model Manager
tools.description: Update Schematics pushes the current library symbol (graphics, pins, parameters, models per the update options) to all placed instances in open schematics, while Model Manager lists every component in the library with its model links in a grid so footprints/simulation models can be added or replaced in bulk (multi-select and Add Footprint).
tools.usage: Schematic Library editor: Tools > Update Schematics; Tools > Model Manager
tools.example: Select all 0402 capacitors in Model Manager, Add Footprint 'CAPC1005X55N' so each gains the alternate footprint.
tools.notes: Update Schematics only touches open sheets; Tools > Update From Libraries in the schematic editor is the pull counterpart.
